name: Algeria
alt: A world map with a huge highlighted country across the top of a continent, mostly covered in a vast desert stretching south.
facts: It's the largest country in Africa by land area.
More than four-fifths of its land is covered by the vast Sahara Desert.
Ancient Roman ruins still stand remarkably intact in several of its desert towns, preserved for centuries by the dry climate.

name: Angola
alt: A world map with a highlighted country along the southwestern coast of a continent, facing a wide ocean.
facts: Portuguese is its official language, a legacy of centuries of colonial rule.
It's one of the largest oil producers on the continent, alongside rich diamond deposits.
One of its waterfalls ranks among the largest in Africa by the sheer volume of water that thunders over it.

name: Benin
alt: A world map with a small, narrow highlighted country running from a short coastline far inland on the western bulge of a continent.
facts: It's considered the birthplace of a spiritual tradition that spread across the Atlantic and shaped religions still practiced in the Americas today.
A powerful kingdom once ruled here for centuries, famous for an all-female regiment of warriors who defended it.
One of its coastal towns has a memorial gate honoring the millions forced onto ships bound for the Americas centuries ago.

name: Botswana
alt: A world map with a landlocked highlighted country in the middle of a continent's southern half, much of it covered in desert.
facts: It's home to one of the largest populations of elephants left in the world.
One of its rivers spreads out into a massive inland delta that never reaches the sea, instead soaking into the desert sands.
Diamonds discovered here decades ago turned it into one of the fastest-growing economies on the continent.

name: Burkina Faso
alt: A world map with a landlocked highlighted country on the western bulge of a continent, surrounded by several neighbors.
facts: It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
Its name translates to roughly 'land of upright people.'
Every two years, one of its cities hosts one of the largest film festivals on the entire continent.

name: Burundi
alt: A world map with a tiny, landlocked highlighted country tucked beside a long lake in the middle of a continent.
facts: It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
It borders one of the deepest and longest freshwater lakes in the world.
A traditional style of ceremonial drumming performed here has been recognized as an important piece of world heritage.

name: Cameroon
alt: A world map with a highlighted country shaped like a long triangle, stretching from a coastline up into the middle of a continent.
facts: It's sometimes nicknamed 'Africa in miniature,' since its landscapes range from beaches to deserts to rainforest to snow-capped peaks.
More than 250 different languages are spoken here, an enormous variety for one country.
Its tallest peak is an active volcano, the highest point in its entire region.

name: Central African Republic
alt: A world map with a landlocked highlighted country in the very middle of a continent, surrounded by many neighbors.
facts: It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
Diamonds and gold lie beneath much of its soil, though plenty of it remains unexplored.
A protected rainforest reserve here is one of the best places on the continent to see forest elephants and gorillas up close.

name: Chad
alt: A world map with a large, landlocked highlighted country in the middle of a continent, stretching from desert in the north to greener land in the south.
facts: It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
Its namesake lake has shrunk to a fraction of its former size over the past several decades.
A remote, rocky plateau in its north is dotted with ancient rock art and dramatic sandstone arches carved by wind.

name: Republic of the Congo
alt: A world map with a highlighted country along the western coast of a continent, much of it covered in dense rainforest.
facts: Most of its land is covered by a vast rainforest, part of the second-largest rainforest on Earth.
Oil exports make up a huge share of its economy, despite its relatively small population.
It shares its name, and a long riverside border, with a much larger neighboring country right across the water.

name: Côte d'Ivoire
alt: A world map with a highlighted country along the southern coast of a continent's western bulge, facing a gulf.
facts: It produces more cocoa, the key ingredient in chocolate, than any other country on Earth.
One of its cities is home to one of the largest churches in the world, modeled after a famous basilica in Europe but built even taller.
Its name comes from a trade in elephant tusks that once thrived along its coast centuries ago.

name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
alt: A world map with a vast highlighted country in the middle of a continent, covered largely by rainforest and crossed by a great river.
facts: It's the second-largest country in Africa by land area.
One of its rivers is the deepest river in the world, plunging far below the surface in places.
It holds a huge share of the world's reserves of a metal that's essential for batteries in phones and electric cars.

name: Djibouti
alt: A world map with a tiny highlighted country at the entrance to a narrow sea, where a continent nearly touches another across the water.
facts: It sits at a narrow, strategically important strait where a sea meets a gulf, making it a hub for international shipping.
One of its lakes is so salty that swimmers float effortlessly, and its shoreline marks the lowest point on the entire continent.
Several foreign countries keep military bases here because of its location along major shipping routes.

name: Egypt
alt: A world map with a highlighted country at the northeastern corner of a continent, with a thin green river valley cutting through a vast desert.
facts: It's home to the last surviving wonder of the ancient world, a massive stone pyramid built more than 4,500 years ago.
A canal cut through its land lets ships travel between two seas without sailing all the way around an entire continent.
The world's longest river flows north through nearly its whole length before reaching the sea.

name: Equatorial Guinea
alt: A world map with a tiny highlighted country split between a sliver of mainland and a few small islands in a gulf.
facts: It's the only country in Africa where Spanish is an official language.
It's split between a piece of mainland and a handful of islands out in a nearby gulf.
Oil discovered offshore decades ago transformed it into one of the wealthiest countries on the continent per person.

name: Eritrea
alt: A world map with a highlighted country along a narrow sea on the eastern edge of a continent.
facts: Its capital is filled with striking Art Deco buildings left behind by colonizers nearly a century ago, earning it UNESCO recognition.
Its coastline runs along a long, narrow sea connecting to a famous canal far to the north.
A scattered group of islands off its coast remains largely untouched, with some visited by only a handful of travelers each year.

name: Ethiopia
alt: A world map with a large, landlocked highlighted country in the eastern part of a continent, covered in rugged highlands.
facts: It's considered the birthplace of coffee, where wild coffee plants were first discovered growing.
It uses its own calendar, which runs several years behind the one used in most of the rest of the world.
An entire complex of churches in one of its towns was carved directly downward out of solid rock, rather than built upward from the ground.

name: Gabon
alt: A world map with a highlighted country along the western coast of a continent, straddling the equator and covered almost entirely in rainforest.
facts: More than four-fifths of its land is covered by dense rainforest.
It has one of the lowest population densities on the continent, leaving huge stretches of wilderness untouched.
One of its national parks is nicknamed 'Africa's Last Eden' for its rare mix of forest elephants, gorillas, and even hippos that wander onto beaches.

name: Gambia
alt: A world map with a tiny, thin ribbon of a highlighted country following a river inland from the coast, almost entirely surrounded by one neighbor.
facts: It's the smallest country on mainland Africa.
It's shaped like a long, thin ribbon, following the curves of a river that gives it its name.
It's almost entirely surrounded by a single much larger neighboring country, except for a short stretch of coastline.

name: Ghana
alt: A world map with a highlighted country along the southern coast of a continent's western bulge, facing a gulf.
facts: It was the first country in sub-Saharan Africa to gain independence from colonial rule.
One of its lakes is the largest reservoir in the world by surface area, created by a massive dam.
For centuries, the wealth of gold mined and traded here gave the region one of its old European nicknames.

name: Guinea
alt: A world map with a highlighted country curving along the western coast of a continent, rising into highlands inland.
facts: It holds some of the largest reserves of the ore used to make aluminum found anywhere on Earth.
Several major rivers that flow through neighboring countries all begin in its highlands, earning it a nickname as a regional 'water tower.'
Its coastline and inland mountains create dramatically different climates within a fairly small country.

name: Guinea-Bissau
alt: A world map with a small highlighted country along the western coast of a continent, fringed by a scatter of small islands.
facts: Portuguese is its official language, left over from centuries of colonial rule.
An archipelago of dozens of islands off its coast is protected as a UNESCO biosphere reserve, home to saltwater hippos and nesting sea turtles.
Cashew nuts make up the vast majority of everything it exports to the rest of the world.

name: Kenya
alt: A world map with a highlighted country straddling the equator on the eastern side of a continent, facing a warm ocean.
facts: The equator runs directly through it, splitting it almost evenly between two hemispheres.
Every year, millions of wildebeest and zebra cross through its grasslands in one of the largest animal migrations on Earth.
Runners from here have won an extraordinary number of major long-distance races and Olympic medals for the size of the country.

name: Lesotho
alt: A world map with a small highlighted country completely surrounded by a single much larger neighbor, near the southern tip of a continent.
facts: It's completely surrounded on all sides by a single other country, with no other neighbors at all.
Its lowest point is still higher above sea level than the highest point in many other countries.
Many of its mountain villages can only be reached by horse or on foot during heavy snow.

name: Liberia
alt: A world map with a highlighted country along the southern coast of a continent's western bulge, facing a wide ocean.
facts: It was founded in the 1800s by formerly enslaved people who had gained their freedom and sailed back across the ocean.
Its name comes from the word 'liberty.'
It's one of the oldest republics on the entire continent, having declared independence in the mid-1800s.

name: Libya
alt: A world map with a large highlighted country along the northern coast of a continent, almost entirely covered by desert.
facts: More than nine-tenths of its land is covered by desert.
It holds some of the largest oil reserves on the entire continent.
Decades ago, it built a massive network of pipelines to pump ancient underground water hundreds of miles to its dry coastal cities.

name: Madagascar
alt: A world map with a long highlighted island off the southeastern coast of a continent, separated by a wide channel of sea.
facts: It's the fourth-largest island in the world.
About 90 percent of the plants and animals found here exist nowhere else on Earth, including every species of lemur.
It split away from mainland Africa so long ago that its wildlife evolved on its own for tens of millions of years.

name: Malawi
alt: A world map with a long, narrow, landlocked highlighted country wrapped around one side of a great lake in the southern part of a continent.
facts: It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
One enormous lake covers about a fifth of its total area, and is home to more species of fish than almost any other lake on Earth.
It's nicknamed the 'Warm Heart of Africa,' known for how friendly and welcoming people here are to visitors.

name: Mali
alt: A world map with a large, landlocked highlighted country in the western part of a continent, stretching from desert in the north to greener land along a river in the south.
facts: It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
One of its ancient cities became so legendary as a center of gold, salt, and learning that its name is still used to describe any far-off, mysterious place.
A great river curves through its southern half, the only reliable water source across a vast stretch of desert.

name: Mauritania
alt: A world map with a large highlighted country along the western coast of a continent, almost entirely covered by desert.
facts: About 90 percent of its land is covered by the Sahara Desert.
A bizarre, perfectly circular rock formation in its desert is so large and strange that it's nicknamed the 'Eye of the Sahara' and can be spotted from space.
A famous old desert railway here pulls trains so long that some stretch for more than a mile and a half hauling iron ore.

name: Morocco
alt: A world map with a highlighted country at the northwestern corner of a continent, just across a narrow strait from another continent.
facts: At its closest point, it sits less than 10 miles across a narrow strait from a country on a different continent entirely.
One of its mountain towns is painted almost entirely in shades of blue, from its walls to its doorways to its stairs.
Its rugged mountain range runs for hundreds of miles, separating fertile coastal plains from the Sahara Desert beyond.

name: Mozambique
alt: A world map with a long highlighted country along the southeastern coast of a continent, facing a warm ocean channel.
facts: Portuguese is its official language, a legacy of centuries of colonial rule.
Its long coastline along a warm ocean is dotted with island archipelagos popular for diving and snorkeling.
One of its national parks, once devastated by decades of war, has seen its wildlife dramatically recover through major conservation efforts.

name: Namibia
alt: A world map with a highlighted country along the southwestern coast of a continent, fronted by a stretch of desert coastline.
facts: It has one of the lowest population densities of any country in the world.
It's home to one of the oldest deserts on Earth, famous for towering, rust-red sand dunes.
A stretch of its Atlantic coastline is littered with old shipwrecks and is nicknamed for the bones found scattered along its shores.

name: Niger
alt: A world map with a large, landlocked highlighted country in the western part of a continent, mostly covered in desert.
facts: It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
Much of its territory lies within the Sahara Desert, making it one of the hottest countries on Earth.
A great river that gives the country its name cuts through its southwestern corner, the only major water source across a vast desert landscape.

name: Nigeria
alt: A world map with a highlighted country on the southern coast of a continent's western bulge, facing a gulf.
facts: It's the most populous country on the entire continent.
Its film industry produces more movies per year than almost any other country on Earth, trailing only one other.
It's home to one of the largest economies on the continent, fueled in large part by oil.

name: Rwanda
alt: A world map with a tiny, landlocked highlighted country in the middle of a continent, covered in rolling green hills.
facts: It's nicknamed the 'Land of a Thousand Hills' for its endlessly rolling, green terrain.
It's one of the best places on Earth to see endangered mountain gorillas living wild in misty forests.
Once a month, nearly the entire country pauses for a national clean-up day, with everyone pitching in to tidy public spaces.

name: South Sudan
alt: A world map with a landlocked highlighted country in the eastern part of a continent, crossed by a great river and its swampy wetlands.
facts: It's the newest country in the world, gaining independence only in 2011.
It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
A vast, swampy wetland here is one of the largest in the world, fed by a great river winding through reeds and grasses.

name: Senegal
alt: A world map with a highlighted country at the westernmost point of a continent's mainland, wrapped almost entirely around a smaller neighbor.
facts: It includes the westernmost point on mainland Africa.
One of its small islands served as a major departure point during a centuries-long slave trade and is now a solemn memorial.
One of its lakes turns a striking shade of pink because of algae that thrive in its salty water.

name: Sierra Leone
alt: A world map with a small highlighted country along the western coast of a continent, facing a wide ocean.
facts: Its capital was founded centuries ago as a settlement for formerly enslaved people resettled from across the ocean.
Diamonds mined here have at times fueled conflict, but also represent some of its greatest natural wealth.
Its capital is one of the rainiest capital cities in the world, with downpours lasting much of the year.

name: Somalia
alt: A world map with a highlighted country curving around the easternmost point of a continent, with a long coastline facing two different bodies of water.
facts: It has the longest coastline of any country on mainland Africa.
For thousands of years, traders here exported fragrant tree resins so valuable that ancient civilizations used them in religious rituals and embalming.
Many people here still follow a traditional nomadic lifestyle, herding camels and livestock across dry plains.

name: South Africa
alt: A world map with a highlighted country at the very southern tip of a continent, wrapping around a smaller landlocked neighbor.
facts: It has three separate capital cities, each handling a different branch of government.
It officially recognizes 12 languages, more than almost any other country in the world.
One of its national parks is one of the largest wildlife reserves in Africa, home to all of the 'big five' animals safari-goers hope to spot.

name: Sudan
alt: A world map with a large highlighted country in the northeastern part of a continent, crossed by two branches of a great river that join together.
facts: It's home to more ancient pyramids than its more famous northern neighbor, even though they're smaller and less visited.
Its capital sits at the exact spot where two great branches of the world's longest river join together.
Much of its land lies within the Sahara Desert, though a long coastline along a narrow sea lines its northeast.

name: Tanzania
alt: A world map with a highlighted country on the eastern coast of a continent, home to its tallest peak and several great lakes.
facts: It's home to the tallest mountain on the entire continent, snow-capped despite being near the equator.
Vast herds of wildebeest and zebra cross its grasslands every year in one of the largest wildlife migrations on Earth.
A cluster of islands off its coast has been nicknamed the 'Spice Islands' for centuries of trading cloves, nutmeg, and cinnamon.

name: Togo
alt: A world map with a long, narrow highlighted country running from a short coastline far inland on the western bulge of a continent.
facts: It's a long, narrow country, stretching from a short stretch of coastline far inland.
Traditional religious practices rooted in spirit worship remain widely followed alongside other faiths.
Its sandy beaches are lined with coconut palms along a stretch of the Gulf of Guinea.

name: Tunisia
alt: A world map with a small highlighted country at the northern tip of a continent, jutting out into a sea.
facts: It's the smallest country in its region of North Africa.
One of history's most powerful ancient trading civilizations was based in a city near its modern capital, before it was eventually destroyed by a rival empire.
Its desert landscapes were used to film the deserts of a fictional faraway planet in a famous movie series.

name: Uganda
alt: A world map with a landlocked highlighted country in the eastern part of a continent, bordering one of its largest lakes.
facts: It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
The world's longest river begins its journey here, flowing out of one of Africa's largest lakes.
It's nicknamed the 'Pearl of Africa' for its lush, green landscapes and abundant wildlife.

name: Zambia
alt: A world map with a landlocked highlighted country in the southern part of a continent, shaped like a butterfly.
facts: It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
It shares one of the largest waterfalls in the world with a neighboring country, where a mighty river plunges over a cliff in a thunderous curtain of mist.
Copper mined from beneath its soil has powered its economy for generations.

name: Zimbabwe
alt: A world map with a landlocked highlighted country in the southern part of a continent, bordered by a great river to its north.
facts: Its name comes from a massive ancient stone-walled city built by its ancestors centuries ago, the ruins of which still stand today.
It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
It shares one of the largest waterfalls in the world with a neighboring country, fed by a mighty river that plunges over a cliff in a thunderous curtain of mist.

name: Eswatini
alt: A world map with a tiny, landlocked highlighted country tucked into the southeastern corner of a continent, surrounded by larger neighbors.
facts: It's one of the last countries in the world ruled by an absolute monarch with sweeping personal power.
It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
It officially changed its name a few years back, dropping an older name that some felt was too easily confused with a country on a different continent.
